newsitem.title: USA: S&P warns of fallout from Calif.'s Proposition 218.
newsitem.headline: S&P warns of fallout from Calif.'s Proposition 218.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp warned on Monday that many local governments in California could experience credit erosion over time because of Proposition 218, a controversial tax reform measure approved last November by the state's voters.
Proposition 218 requires voter approval of an array of taxes, assessments and fees levied by local governments.

"Many governments are likely to see reduced financial flexibility and possible credit erosion over time because of the measure's increased obstacles standing in the way of future service and infrastructure needs," S&P said in its CreditWeek Municipal newsletter.

Despite the uncertainty, S&P said it continues to rate bonds and other securities that have potential Proposition 218 questions, including assessment district bonds, special tax bonds and utility revenue bonds.
The rating agency said its overall approach is to rate securities in a manner that conforms with a "consensus and reasonable" interpretation of the initiative.
S&P said it expects to evaluate the impact of Proposition 218 on issuers on a case-by-case basis. It said the creditworthiness of many California issuers is likely to come under pressure.
S&P has already reduced one rating as a result of the initiative's passage -- San Diego's general obligation bonds.
